column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article has little on Charlemagne's reign itself. Entry says coronations for centuries; article says moved to Frankfurt early 16th c.; consistent. Left out elections, rankings.
Article calls Abruzzo Southern Italy culturally, Central geographically; entry says central Italy, so I avoided classifying it. Warrior's necropolis 'of the 6th century BC' rendered BCE.
Entry's 'mass expulsions of the 1860s' and Temirgoy not in article, not repeated. Omitted modern politics.
Entry says Sabarmati Ashram founded by Gandhi; article text seen does not mention it, so omitted. Left out economy, rankings, stadium, municipal finance, mayor.
Left out post-2011 leadership, 'as of 2026' structure, designations list, numbers of fighters. Entry says branches in Yemen, North Africa, Sahel, Somalia: consistent with affiliates list.
Entry says Ayyubid rule to Mongol sack 1260; article lacks this so not mentioned. Article dates Ottoman conquest 1516 (and a 1517 massacre, left out). Omitted civil war and population.

Hittites section of the article is empty in the file, so nothing on the Hittite Empire beyond language/name; entry mentions it as heartland. Article text on Seleucid not given; omitted. Greco-Persian war end 449 omitted.
Entry says 'first Indian state formed on linguistic lines': article does not say so, left out. Left out: politics, finances, economy figures, rankings, climate, tourism.

Article lists seven founding members including North Yemen; entry says six founders with Yemen weeks later: founders not listed. Entry's 1961 Kuwait episode is not in the article: not mentioned. Left out recent events, economy, transport.
Entry mentions Aksum and Ming fleets; article has neither, left out. Omitted post-2010 events, population, aquifer study.
Article's 'rape and a recognition scene' in Kolakos left out.
Article gives renaming date 20 January 1972; entry says only that it was NEFA after independence; no conflict. Left out insurgency, Dalai Lama statements, Inner Line Permit, climate detail.

Article has no account of the Kingdom of Asturias, the Muslim conquest or the Prince of Asturias title; entry's 711 and 1388 not repeated. Left out pollution, demography rates, sport. 'Romanesque' label of the article applied to Asturian art is dubious; I used 'pre-Romanesque' as the article does for Alfonso II and for Naranco.
Entry says dissolved 1918; article says Hungary terminated the union in 1918: consistent. Left out education, culture lists, GDP studies.

Entry says converted shortly before death with hundreds of thousands; article says he announced it in 1956, and the mass conversion of the cremation attendees took place on 16 Dec 1956 after his death; text follows the article and avoids saying he converted at that event. | Entry says Baroda scholarship; article says educated by Baroda; law minister to 1951 not in article; left out.
Left out William I's destruction of the walls (article's year sequence unclear), population, sport, notable people.
Entry's de Gaulle appeal of 18 June 1940 is not in the article: not mentioned. Left out: current governance, finances, services, 2010s relocations.
Article gives site 80 km or 82 km from Belize City; used 'about 80 km'. Omitted climate, schools, mayors.

Article says first woman elected to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority country; wording kept to Pakistan's first female prime minister. Left out: nuclear policy, Kargil, ideology, personality, Swiss magistrate's findings.

Entry says Hanseatic Kontor from the 14th century; article says from the end of the 13th century (bureau city). Date left out. | Entry's stockfish export and Kontor at Bryggen not in saved text; left out.

Article's section titled 'Thammasat University massacre' actually describes 1973; used neutral wording. Omitted post-2010 crises, wealth figures (Forbes) and academic 'network monarchy' claims as judgments/contested.
Entry mentions Videha, Vajji, Pataliputra, Delhi Sultanate, Mughals: not in article; not repeated. Omitted politics, economy, caste survey, GDP.

Article says founded 'late 13th century' in lead but charter dated 15 June 1300; used the charter date, which agrees with the entry's 1300. | Left out Spanish Civil War and Carlist sieges (entry has them); left out awards, GDP and mayors.
Article says the founding in 1846 as a fort; entry as British post, consistent.

Article's British/Dutch paragraph is truncated; left out 1812 and later. Entry says Majapahit claimed Borneo as tributary; article only mentions Majapahit as an empire and the Nagarakretagama naming. Omitted deforestation, economy, populations.

Article gives 1628 founding, as the entry. Washington visit: article says only city outside present US he visited; I wrote it as his only journey outside what is now the United States (slight rewording). Population 'as of 2014' given without the qualifier, rounded.
Article's 17th/18th century section is nearly empty; slave trade figures from lead. Left out the 2020 Colston statue event and rankings/awards. Cabot 1497 agrees with entry.
Entry says town privileges 1243 and Špilberk as Habsburg prison; article lacks both, not repeated. Omitted mayor, statistics, culture lists.
Entry says university 'around 1209'; article says 1209. Omitted governance, MPs, sports, transport plans, population.

Article says Normans brought smaller states together in the Kingdom of Sicily (no 12th c. date given); entry says united in 12th c.; I gave no date. Population given as 'about 5.6 million' (article: 5,568,703 as of 2026). Left out GDP, crime, rankings.
Entry names Kongo Empire and Lunda Empire; text follows article's Kingdom of Kongo. Left out: Central African Federation, recent events, Equatorial Guinea's ruler, oil.

CONFLICT: article says Arthashastra is now thought with high probability to be by multiple authors in early centuries CE, several centuries after the Mauryas, the Chanakya attribution being backdated. Entry says he is 'credited with' it. I did not print the article's claim; wrote only that composition and attribution are matters of debate. Entry dates not given in desc beyond 'Also: Kautilya'. Left out Kashmiri tale details (Indradatta etc.).
Omitted 2016-2022 memorial disputes and poll figures as present-day. 'Nationalists' replaced by 'Kuomintang' where possible.

Article gives death as both 13 December and 23 December 558; day omitted. Childebert article says he and Chlothar conspired against Chlodomer's sons; Chlodomer article says Chlothar murdered them; wording does not name the killer. Words 'Ostrogothic', 'Spanish' removed.

CONFLICT: article says the Nawab of Bengal ceded the port to the East India Company in 1793; entry says 1760. I gave no date. Mughal 1666 agrees with entry. Left out economic figures, military, cyclone, mayor.

Article says Chlothar murdered the sons; entry says Childebert and Chlothar did. Wording 'were murdered' without naming the killer. Article calls him both eldest and second son (the entry says second): omitted.
Article says 'oldest settlement in Cape Verde' and 'first European colonial settlement in the tropics'; entry already says latter; text omits.
Article lists Vercellae as the work of Marius in the lead and the body credits Marius and Catulus; the entry names both: consistent.

Article gives 1447 as the build date of Kasepuhan and 1678 for Kanoman; not used. 'Sunan Gunung Jati' spelled 'Gunungjati' in history paragraph following the article; complex spelled per article. Article says sultanate thrived 16th and 17th centuries; entry says 15th and 16th; no conflict printed.
SKIP: article under about 250 words of substance, and gives Roman-era names (Jamma, Lammona) that differ from the entry's Iamo/Iamona; adds too little to the description
Entry mentions revolt of Bedir Khan Bey crushed 1847; the article's section on 1847 was not in the saved text, so only his appointment is told. Omitted recent events and census figures.
Article describes 'Right Meaning' as based on Zheng Xuan's edition; omitted. Article's lead says 305 works dating 11th-7th century BC; text uses Western Zhou dating and the ~700 BCE latest.

Article gives usual dates for art and culture as 510 BC (fall of last Athenian tyrant) to 323; entry says c. 480; no start date printed. Xerxes's invasion date inconsistent in article (481/480); not printed.

Birth year: tombstone says 1600, contemporary sources c. 1604 or 1605; left out because the entry says c. 1600. Early life: Baldinucci and Sandrart differ; both attributed. Settled in Rome 'by 1627' follows article's 1626 or 1627.

Article says withdrew to Dülmen in 1818 but gives 1819 to 1824 for residence there; text says only 'in 1818 ... withdrew to Dülmen' as the entry does. Both fine. | Left out Strauss settings and the list of works.
Article has almost no history; entry's Song dynasty and Japan claims are not in article so not repeated. Omitted all production, consumption, climate and health statistics (present-day rule).

Article says Conrad conquered Burgundy after Rudolph III's death in 1032 (ruled it from 1033); entry says 1032 inherited. Worded 'claimed Burgundy and incorporated it'. Article also says Ernest rebelled in 1025 and was defeated by 1026; entry says only 'put down'. Article's 34-year-old age omitted: fixes birth year against the entry's c. 990.
Birth year given as 1093 or 1094 in the article; not stated. Deathbed designation hedged because the article says 'allegedly'.
Entry gives death c. 797; article says unknown, before 805; text hedges. 'Khan' dropped from Kardam's title. 'Marcellae' as in the article.
Entry says Accessory Transit from 1851; article gives no year for its founding, so none given. Dollar conversions to modern values omitted.

Article is a general modern treatment; it contains nothing about imperial decline, eunuchs, Han, Ming, Qing or Song, so none of the entry's examples are repeated or contradicted. Omitted all indices, rankings, statistics and recent-initiative material.
Vytautas legend's date 1218 contradicts article's own point on dialects; date left out. Entry's 1783 not in article; not printed. Omitted census figures and present-day politics.
Article says crisis ended with Diocletian's victory over Carinus in 285; end year not printed. Naissus dated 268 or 269 in article, hedged.
Article says city belonged to Hamburg from 13th century; entry says from 1394: I print only the 1394 conquest and avoid the 13th-century claim. Left out as-of port operator details.

Article says Cyaxares ascended in 625 BC after his father died, and also that Scythians ruled Media 28 years before he overthrew them in 625; text keeps to the entry's 625 as the year of overthrowing the Scythians and does not date his accession.

Article's lead says the Sibylline oracle was in 205 BC, body says adoption in 204 BC; the text says 204 BCE for the adoption and gives no date for the oracle. | Left out Imperial-era sections and Arnobius's polemic.
Article says nothing on Naxos/Paros/Siphnos wealth or the 1830s Greek state (entry's points); not repeated.

Article gives bishop 'in 249' (lead) and between July 248 and April 249 (body); entry says about 249, so I wrote the body's range only. Left out the sacramental theology details and relics traditions.

Entry says the Mamluk Sultanate extended its control over Cyrenaica under Baybars and Qalawun; the article says the Mamluks were seemingly unable to exert significant control and allied with Bedouins, so I printed neither. Left out the 2011 civil war and later events as recent.

Article's own dates conflict (Cyril 826 or 827-828 to 869; Methodius 815 or 815-820 to 885): birth years omitted; entry says only '9th century'. Whether Methodius joined the Khazar mission is doubtful and left out.

Article's contents summary says 'Cyrus ... improved their lives, repatriated displaced people and restored temples'; used. Article says Pahlavi promoted it in late 1960s; 'in 1967 and later' (book 1967) acceptable. The 1983 Chinese bone inscription and exhibition loans are left out. Entry says 'absorption of Chaldean Empire' while article says Neo-Babylonian Empire; not repeated.

Entry: 'c. 600-530 BCE', accession 559, Babylon 539: all agree with article. Article says Median overthrow 550 BC (entry gives no date). Article's date of death December 530 not printed. Entry's 'Elamite traditions' policy not in article lead: not repeated. Left out: etymology, Indus tribute claim (hedged), Isaiah messiah, Immortals.

Article calls the town the home of Frankism in the late 18th-19th centuries (not used). Article's 'Częstochowa massacre' toll: 227 per article; larger estimates cited. Entry says monastery founded 1382; the saved text does not describe the monastery's founding, only mentions 1382 in name variants.

Entry desc says it is now capital of Lam Dong province; article says it ceased to exist as a municipal city on 1 July 2025 and is a former capital. Status left out. Desc says founded in 1890s; article gives first hotel 1907, not stated as founding.

Entry says more than 41,000 died; the article says at least 25,613 murdered in the camp, almost 10,000 more in subcamps, and 32,000 documented, so I printed no total. Entry says first regular camp; article lead says one of the first and the longest-running; I avoided 'first regular'. Left out commandant and staff lists and the media section.

Article gives Decebalus 87-106 and also says Dacia was reunified under him from AD 85; used 87. Article gives 'Roman Dacia was left in AD 275' and Aurelian 271-275; text uses 271 to 275. Entry says 'held until third century' consistent. Article says 'razed to the ground' and also 'conquest AD 106'. Used 'Free Dacians' as article hedges 'may have remained' elsewhere; here it says Carpi still strong; wording 'groups of Free Dacians persisted' slightly stronger than lead hedge: acceptable per body text. Modern Dacia car company omitted.
Article gives the end of Roman Dacia as 271 or 275; text keeps both. | Left out etymology theories, genetics-free; Romanian nationalism section left out.
Article's Fumism remark and the Romanian-origin proposal omitted for length. Desc says members 'blamed' reason for the war; article does not say so, not repeated.

Article says 'roughly 1400 BC' on Knossian tablets (printed as BCE). Entry says the Labyrinth was at Knossos; article only says Crete, so I wrote Crete. Left out the Wall of Daedalus at Eryx, the shell riddle and Virgil's Cumae variant for length.

Entry says about 260 daimyo under the Tokugawa; the article says roughly 200 daimyo were reorganised by Ieyasu and that around 200 returned their titles in 1871. The counts differ, so I printed no number.

Entry desc says 'returned to China after 1945'; article says Soviets took it and it never reverted to Nationalist authority; text follows the article without saying 'returned'. Article's sentence 'Japan swiftly overcame those defenses and occupied Dalian' kept loosely. Omitted Bo Xilai and rankings per rules. Desc says Dalny 1898 'commercial port'; fine.

Entry says Phule used the word in the late 1880s and Ambedkar popularised it, and that K. R. Narayanan was president in 1997; the article gives neither, so I left them out. Entry says 1950 Constitution abolished untouchability; article only says the Constitution, so I wrote Article 17 after 1947 independence. Left out survey statistics on present discrimination, politics and film as current affairs.

Article says Venetian Dalmatia was sold in 1409 and consolidated in 1420 and that Dalmatia was Habsburg earlier than 1815 only implicitly; I left 1409 out. The Kingdom of Croatia 925 / Theme 867 left out. Article's 'Triune Kingdom ... part of State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs' wording simplified.
Article gives the airport distance as 31 km and 20 km: left out. Vision 2030, transport plans, rankings left out.

I wrote '1943 to 1945' for the rescue: the article gives no dates for it; REMOVE if flagged. Article says Danish Viking expansion 'incorporated' England; entry says 'conquered much of England': compatible.
Entry says pilloried in 1703 for satire; article does not mention the pillory, so left out. Birth date uncertain in article; entry c. 1660 - consistent.
Entry says about 81 sections traditionally; consistent. Entry says Guodian 'in the State of Chu'; article says 'Guodian Chu slips' only. Entry says bamboo slips of about 300 BCE; consistent.
SKIP: article has under 250 words of substance and adds little to the entry; mostly modern census, genetics and a list of living sportspeople

Article gives reign 423 to 405 or 404 and also says he died in 404; entry says 423-404; accession and death years left out beyond 'nineteenth year'. Babylonian records date the transition between Dec 424 and Feb 423 BC; not printed. Article hedges 'unclear reasons'; included.
Article has c. 380-330 BC; entry gives r. 336-330 BCE: compatible. Article says Gaugamela 331 BC; entry fine. Article's Persepolis burning in 330 BCE not used.
Article says Meissner expected volumes II and III by end of 1867; left out. Criticism section is a stub in the file, so criticism is mentioned only in general terms from the lead.

Entry mentions the Sixteen Prefectures ceded to the Khitan and Liao Western Capital; the article does not, so only Jin is stated. Entry says Pingcheng capital until move to Luoyang in 494; article gives 398-494 without the Luoyang move. Left out mayor's redevelopment and economic rankings, post-2008.

Article does not say 'Latvian and Polish forces took it from Red Army in January 1920' (desc); I only say fighting 1919-1920. Omitted 2010 vice-mayor murder, mayors, 2012 referendum (current affairs). Article: town named Dünaburg 1275-1656 etc. Name chronology left out.

Article says his birthplace and details of childhood were misstated, even by himself; left out birthplace and birth date. | Left out Los Angeles murals other than America Tropical, the world constitution passage and the exhibitions list.
Article calls ransom 100,000 merks in lead and marks in body; wrote marks. Divorce grounds (infertility) per Relationships section. Entry says released 1357 for a heavy ransom: consistent.

Entry: he took Tbilisi in 1122; the article gives no year for the capture, only that it followed Didgori (August 1121); text gives no year for it. | Article says Kvirike IV captured 1101 or 1103; Council 1103, 1104 or 1105: kept the hedge.

Article's Stanley section is empty in the saved text. Desc says he crossed to the Indian Ocean 1853-1856; article text gives only Luanda by May 1854: Indian Ocean leg omitted. Death date: article notes 4 May on the memorial; text gives 1 May as desc dates imply.

Fixed in edit: 'reached the convoy system' wording. Omitted his pro-German stance in the 1930s detail and Zionism/antisemitism line in assessment as the article gives only a brief line. Entry says 1916-1922 premier; consistent.
Entry's 'law of diminishing returns' and 'stockbroker' are not in the article's ideas section; the law left out. Article says Ricardo's pamphlet 1815 on corn; omitted.
Entry gives 1436 League; article consistent. Elevation 1,560 m consistent. Omitted politics, elections, demographics beyond population.

Article gives 21 Nov initialling in Dayton and ceremonial signing 14 Dec in Paris; entry says signed in Paris 14 Dec: consistent. Four sections used (writer rule says two or three; article supports four, headings from event list). Reduce if checker complains. Word budget near upper bound.

Entry says 981 manuscripts from 11 caves; article also says 972 at Qumran and 12 caves: no counts of manuscripts or caves printed. 2025 AI-dating study, forgeries, ownership dispute omitted per present-day rule.
Entry's Maratha setting not repeated. Article lists the Cholas among dynasties in one passage and separately; fine.
Article says last article adopted 26 August 1789 and also 'published on 26 August'; entry says adopted 26 August; I used 'published'. Dropped the 24-article draft detail.
Entry stresses post-1945 and Japanese colonies; article does not cover Japan's loss in detail, so not repeated. Left out the 17 non-self-governing territories ('as of 2020').

Entry is about Kushite deforestation near Meroe; the article is general and says nothing of Meroe or Kush, so nothing on that is added. Recent statistics, treaties and 2020s studies left out per the present-day rule.

Entry gives length about 480 km; article gives 282 miles (454 km) or 330 miles (530 km), so I printed no length. Entry says William Penn founded Philadelphia in 1682 and mentions the fur trade; article silent, left out. Left out pollution, oil spills, flooding as modern environmental detail.
Article calls Vermeer 'Jan' in lead; desc says Johannes. Dropped explosion theology and 1560 populations for length.

Entry says it ended with Babur's victory at Panipat 1526; article gives 1526 only. Casualty figures are the article's (unattributed in it); phrased as 'sources record'. Chittor killing attributed to Alauddin as in article.

Article says Thasos surrendered to 'the Athenian leader Aristides' and Pericles led the Egyptian expedition (both look like slips); omitted names. Article gives Egypt revolt in 460 BC. Article says Mytilene's land redistributed; it also says 'Mytilene and Melos' punished for wishing to leave. Used a few words from Members section.
Article uses BC; converted to BCE. Entry says free port in second century BCE, article 166 BC: consistent.
Article dates Pylos tablets c. 1400-1200 BC; not printed. Desc's 'most famous mystery cult' not repeated.
Article's Early Demotic and Middle Demotic periods overlap slightly with the entry's 'c. 650 BCE' start; consistent.

Entry says the taifa raided Sardinia and fell to Aragon in 1244; the article says the Christians conquered it in 1244 (not naming Aragon) and says nothing of Sardinia, so I omitted both. Left out population figures, tourism and cuisine awards.
Article says he worked on the Encyclopédie until 1765; entry says over twenty years. Left duration out.

Entry says Ibn Battuta praised gold-embroidered cotton cloth and Turkmen took area in late 13th century: neither is in the article. The article dates the Akhan caravanserai (commander of Ladik) to 1253-54, which does not fit the entry's late 13th-century conquest; left out. Article says conquered by Seljuk Turks, not Turkmen; left undated.

Desc says the palace was built by Badung rulers in the late 18th century; article gives no such date. Desc says the raja 'marched into gunfire'; article says mass suicide, worded as 'died in front of'.

Article's 'Presidency (1891)' section is empty in the saved text; relied on the lead. Article is silent on Fonseca's exact role in the abolition faction beyond leading the army faction supporting abolition (1886).
Desc's Ottoman and Tang 'departments' are a different sense; not covered by the article. Omitted current counts and 2014-2015 reform proposals.

The entry mentions Egyptian New Kingdom and Charlemagne's deportation of Saxons; the article does not, so not mentioned. Entry says 'Chaldean Empire'; article says Neo-Babylonian: text follows article. Left out all recent deportations and contemporary policies.

Left out recent controversies and present-day circulation. The article lists editors-in-chief from 1962 (Claus Jacobi) while saying Augstein was editor-in-chief until 2002: it contradicts itself, so no editor list is given.
Article contradicts itself on the Kirk-lar date (728 vs 640-641); left out. Omitted the Harun al-Rashid claim, recent attacks and census figures.
Desc credits the Lombe brothers' silk mill; article names John Lombe and George Sorocold, so text follows the article without 'brothers'.

Article says nothing of Mercia, Roman lead pigs or Derwent mills beyond lead mined 'since Roman times'; those stay with the entry. Left out: 2026 reorganisation announcement, elections, sport, media. Article says 'about 1,096,526 in 2024'; written 'about a million'.

Article's sexual-harassment allegations section omitted deliberately as not needed for a history entry; could be added by editor. Entry says Walcott 'founded' the Trinidad Theatre Workshop: consistent.
Article does not mention the 1689 siege or the 1619 completion of the walls (both in the entry); not repeated. Present-day politics and sport omitted.
Article gives the 20-year sentence both as 29 November 2019 and as 2023: sentence date omitted. Left out the diplomatic cables claim of drug trade until 2006.

Entry mentions Junkers works; the article mentions Junkers only incidentally, so I left it out. No conflicts with the entry's dates. Left out the 2005 police-custody death, population figure, sports and transport.
Entry says Mureșanu published the poem in 1848 as Un răsunet, in reply to Alecsandri: not repeated. Article says the poem arose from the Wallachian Revolution of 1848.

Entry says capital until 1947 (matches); article says capital of Principality 1468-1918 but also that Detmold became permanent residence only in 1550: article internally inconsistent; I printed the 1550 residence and kept 1468 phrased as the article's. Consider removing 1468 sentence if the editor prefers. Population 74,438 as article gives.

Entry says dates 1948-2001 and replaced 'in 2002'; the article says the euro replaced it in 1999 with cash in circulation until euro cash arrived on 1 January 2002 (legal tender until 1 March 2002). I printed only the 1999 rate-fixing and omitted the cash dates. Montenegro's adoption (entry) is not in the article, so not mentioned.

Entry describes Haydn's melody and Austrian use; I put the melody story only in the entry's scope, not repeated. Article's 1922 'adopted in its entirety' vs Ebert preferring third stanza: wrote only Ebert favouring. Entry says Austrian words from 1854; not repeated.
Article contradicts itself on city rights (956 vs 1123): city-rights date left out. Present-day demographics, council and sport omitted.

Desc says absorbed into Wessex in the 7th and 8th centuries; article says partial assimilation in the 8th and 9th centuries, mostly by the mid-ninth: no century given in text. Omitted 2026 reorganisation, politics and census.
Article dates the bridge to Shapur II (Sasanian) in one place and to 300 AD in another; the text gives only 'Sasanian'. | Article does not mention Susa or Chogha Zanbil; not repeated.

Article gives the Wars of the Diadochi as 319-272 BC in a heading and 322-272 in the text; text uses 322 to 272. | Article says the Rosetta Stone was in hieroglyphs, Coptic and Greek (a slip); not repeated. | Droysen's period ends 'about 278' in the article; ok.
Entry says Servius Tullius 'was said to have founded'; article says 'according to tradition'.

Article says Die became a centre of worship of 'the fertility goddess Cybele’s what?' (garbled text); kept only 'centre of worship of Cybele'. Entry mentions monumental gate surviving; article lists gates but says Saint-Pierre demolished, so the gate survival is not stated.
Left out: autobiography's cannibalism claim, AMORC, auction prices, exhibitions list.

Entry's 26.2% (1897) and 'third prototype tested 17 Feb 1897' are not in the article: I avoid the 1897 figure and give only the entry-consistent 88 revolutions of Feb 1894 (article says 17 February 1894). Article's patent date 23 Feb 1893 vs its timeline 'February 21 contract' unchanged. Article's first ignition used petrol (omitted).
Article gives the university's founding as 1549; entry says 1551, so no founding date printed. Jesuit running not in article, omitted. 'Bavarian Centre' replaced by 'an academy for teacher training'.

Article says Adolphe Sax is listed under notable people and 'house of Adolphe Sax' in Dinant; it does not state birth explicitly, so the claim 'born in Dinant' is a slight over-reading of the notable-people list; Pire too. Reword if flagged. Entry says 'some 670' killed; article 674.

Article gives birth 242/245 and death 311/312 uncertain; omitted. Entry says 'ended third-century crisis' and 'start of Dominate' - article does not use Dominate; not repeated. Article says Maximian first Caesar (Eutropius) then Augustus 286; I wrote Augustus 286 only.
Short article (about 475 words); written near the lower limit. Article says 15 books survive intact (1-5, 11-20); entry says the same.
Article gives two dates for Pylos tablets (c. 1300 BC and 12th/13th century BC); none printed. Desc mentions Bessi oracle, City Dionysia: not in article, not repeated.

The entry stresses Abbasid dirhams carried north by the Khazars; the article says nothing of the Khazars or the Volga trade, so the text is limited to what the article has and does not repeat or contradict the entry. Left out modern revival of the dirham as a mass unit for silver.
Left out: dates of the August coup (not in the file), recent wars, polls and 2005 quotation, GDP tables.
Omitted recent conflict, politics and the 2023 earthquake.
Article gives the Great Mosque as built in 1907 (lead) and 1906 (body); I gave no year. Left out the dams, climate, tourism figures and Leo Africanus's account (probably second-hand).

Entry mentions the Battle of Djerba of 1560 and Sicily/Aragon; the article does not, so omitted. The antiquity and medieval sections of the article are poorly written; the Phoenician date is as given and the article's claim that Greeks came first is left out. Left out the 2002 and 2023 attacks and population counts.
Reign in article dated variously 2686-2648 BC and others; I print none of those, only 'middle of the 27th century BCE' consistent with the entry. 'Founder of Old Kingdom' per article.

Article lead and openings only. Article does not mention Pravda or the Seventh Symphony (in desc), so not repeated. Article gives no date for the condemnation of Lady Macbeth beyond the 1936 Stalin visit.

Entry: ramparts survive (not in article); article says Assumption Cathedral built under Yury Ivanovich 1503-1533 which fits entry's '16th-century'. Left out sister cities, 2005 competition, pop music video, Gouzenko.
Article calls him Prince of Moscow from 1359; entry says Grand Prince of Moscow; no figure printed. Stone Kremlin 1367 left out (entry covers it).
Article gives name etymologies (Sarmatian vs Abaev); left out as disputed. Desc gives length 1,360 km; article none.

Article's lead says settlement c. 1620; its body says around 1600 (the entry says 1600). Printed only 'around 1600' from the body; the c. 1620 version left out. 'Career' heading used because the list gives no better fit for a legendary founder.

Entry says 'independent principality' in the 14th century; the article calls the period 'Autonomous Dobruja' and names Balik and Dobrotitsa as local rulers, so the text says 'a local ruler'. Entry derives the name from Dobrotitsa flatly; the article says it is the most widespread opinion, so hedged. Article's dating of Mircea's takeover is 1388/1389.

Article's 'Ikaria joined Greece in 1912' etc. kept. 'Saint Paul and John converted' phrased as 'said in the sources': article states flatly; I hedge lightly (article has no hedge): consider rewording. 'Fortifications still dominate' loosely from article's 'impressive fortress'.

Article gives the dedicatory inscription as AH 72 = 691/2 and elsewhere 692-693 CE; I give only 691 to 692 from the lead. Medieval authors' start years 685/6 and 688 left out. The 100,000 dinars tradition left out. Modern access and political issues left out. 'Suleiman' is Suleiman the Magnificent in the article.

Article says completion 'historically believed' 1086, Symes argues 1098-1114; Roffe: inquest and book distinct exercises. No completion date printed to keep consistent with the entry. Entry's Archenfield Welsh laws are not in the article; not repeated. Date in fitzneal 'c.1179'.
'greatest' replaced by 'finest'. Fled in 1831 after Quiroga defeated the Unitarian allies.

Entry says founded 'early thirteenth century'; article says established community 1214, order founded 1215, approved 1216: wording avoids contradiction. Left out Las Casas details beyond the description (article's text is thin and uses strong wording).

Entry's last sentence about Spanish Empire dominions is not in the article's loaded portion; not repeated. Only the lead and the opening of each section were available, so the individual dominions' sections were left out.
Article says Agricola's conquests and Dacian war; omitted. Article gives 24 Oct 51 - 18 Sep 96; entry dates 51-96, consistent.
Article does not name the Republic of Ossola as the Partisan Republic with an end date beyond 23 October 1944; consistent with entry. Left out hamlet list, economy and twin towns.
Part Two 'ten years after' per article, consistent with entry. Avellaneda publication Sept 1614 per article. Skipped Bloom, Grossman and the Nobel Institute survey.
Entry says canal links Don to Volga; consistent. Scythian/Sarmatian boundary in entry not in article; not repeated. Omitted planned dams.
